TXT.title: Setup
TXT.welcome_1: Muxwright turns an ADALM-Pluto into a multi-standard test transmitter: DAB+, FM with RDS, DVB-T, DVB-C, DVB-S/S2, PAL and – with a licence – amateur radio DATV.
TXT.welcome_2: In four short steps we check device and firmware, you choose the operating mode and confirm the legal notices. Only then can RF be switched on. The signal chain itself always starts muted.
TXT.dev_hint: You can continue without the firmware – then only DAB+ and FM are available.
TXT.c_pluto_no: No Pluto found – check the USB cable (data cable, not a charge-only cable).
TXT.c_fw_no: Pluto FW {fw}: DAB+ and FM run over USB, DVB-T/C/S/S2 and PAL need the firmware. Copy pluto.frm onto the "PlutoSDR" drive and eject it (optionally test via RAM boot first); reverting to the stock firmware works the same way.
TXT.c_agent_no: Agent at 192.168.2.1:8080 not reachable – replug the Pluto
TXT.c_runner_no: WSL environment "dablab" not reachable – check the installation
TXT.mode_lab_d: Test transmitter for receivers: signals only by cable, attenuator or inside a shielding box. No radiation.
TXT.mode_ham_d: Additionally DATV on amateur bands (QO-100, 13/23/70/6 cm) with your own licence and call sign. Broadcast standards stay shielded.
TXT.callsign_hint: used for station identification in the DATV programme
TXT.legal_hint: Please read each item and confirm it individually.
TXT.done_fw_no_d: DAB+ and FM over USB only
TXT.done_hint: You can reopen the setup at any time via the shield icon at the top right.

shielded: I transmit broadcast signals (DAB+, FM, DVB-T, DVB-C, DVB-S/S2, PAL) only in a shielded setup: by cable with an attenuator, in an RF shielding box or in a test chamber. I use antennas for this only inside the shielding.
no_broadcast_radiation: I am aware that radiating on broadcast, mobile or other assigned frequencies without a frequency assignment from the authority (in Germany the Bundesnetzagentur, TKG) is illegal, can disrupt radio services – including emergency and safety services – and may result in fines or criminal penalties. Outside Germany the local regulations apply.
terms: Muxwright is a lab and development tool, not a certified test instrument, and is provided without warranty. I am responsible for the setup, levels, protection of connected equipment (e.g. a DC block on the satellite input) and compliance with the regulations.
privacy: The dashboard runs locally on this PC and sends no usage or telemetry data. Configuration, media, logs and this confirmation are stored only here (runtime folder). External sources (e.g. YouTube) are only loaded when I select them myself.
ham_license: I hold a valid licence for the amateur radio service (in Germany AFuG/AFuV, otherwise the law of my country) with the call sign given and a class that permits the respective band.
ham_rules: I comply with the band plan, power limits and station identification (call sign in the programme/provider name). Via QO-100 I transmit only according to the transponder rules (AMSAT-DL/BATC), with a suitable amplifier and filtering. Amateur operation applies only to DATV on amateur bands; broadcast standards stay shielded.

HW.intro: What this PC can do live – detected from graphics card, CPU and memory:

rec.uhd_hdr: Recommendation: NVIDIA graphics card from GTX 10xx (Pascal), better RTX – for UHD and HDR10 live.
rec.reserve: Recommendation: a newer NVIDIA RTX card (Turing or later) – more headroom for several UHD programmes; Maxwell/Pascal no longer get new drivers (last branch 580).
rec.ram_low: Recommendation: more memory (16–32 GB), especially for UHD and several programmes.
rec.cpu_low: Recommendation: a stronger CPU (6 cores/12 threads or more) or an NVIDIA graphics card for HD live.

HW.weak: With this hardware it is not guaranteed that frame rate and real time are sufficient for all formats. DAB+, FM and SD always work.
HW.bench_note: The test pattern is easier to encode than real video – real-world values are lower.
HW.shop_intro: Radio, adapters, cables, protection and PC equipment. All shop links are affiliate links (ad).
HW.sponsor_t: Muxwright is a free project. If it helps you, support its development:
HW.log_intro: All events are stored per day (30 days). Messages appear in the selected language; untranslated ones in the original.

COMP.intro: Muxwright contains no codecs and no third-party programs with patent or licence obligations. You install them here yourself from the official sources on this PC: pick a component, read the licence, confirm, "Install".
COMP.patents: Patented technologies (H.264, HEVC, AAC/HE-AAC): private, non-commercial use is patent-free in Germany (§ 11 No. 1 PatG). For commercial use you obtain the licences yourself (Via LA, Access Advance, Sisvel).
COMP.accept: I install this component myself from the source given and have read the licence and notes.
COMP.wsl_missing: WSL is missing: open a command prompt as administrator, run "wsl --install --no-distribution" and restart the PC.
COMP.skip: You can finish the setup before everything is installed – missing standards then stay locked.
COMP.duration: Building ODR-mmbTools and welle-cli takes a few minutes.

desc.wsl_distro: Signal generation runs in its own Ubuntu environment.
desc.odr: DAB+ chain incl. HE-AAC encoder. The FDK-AAC licence grants no patent licence.
desc.welle: Decodes the DAB signal for monitoring.
desc.modulators: DVB-T/C/S/S2 modulators compiled on your PC from the Muxwright source code.
desc.ytdlp: Only needed if you use YouTube videos as a source; respect the platform’s terms of service.
desc.win_ffmpeg: Only for GPU encoding (UHD/HDR10 live) with an NVIDIA graphics card.

legal: Muxwright ships no codecs. In the next step I install FFmpeg, x264/x265, ODR-mmbTools with FDK-AAC, TSDuck and welle-cli myself from the official sources and respect their licences (GPL/LGPL/BSD, FDK-AAC). Private, non-commercial use of patented codecs is permitted in Germany under § 11 No. 1 PatG; for commercial use I obtain the necessary patent licences myself.

FW.intro: DVB-T, DVB-C, DVB-S/S2 and PAL need the Muxwright firmware on the Pluto. It comes tested in the package. The flasher first tests it in RAM only (flash untouched); only then can you write it permanently.
FW.confirm: I understand: flashing overwrites the firmware partition (mtd3). The Pluto must not be unplugged meanwhile. U-Boot and the device settings stay unchanged; a backup is made automatically first.
FW.stop_note: Transmitting is locked during a job; the Pluto is muted and reconnected afterwards.
FW.recovery: Way back: after a RAM test, just unplug USB. After flashing, select the backup and flash it again, or copy the .frm file from runtime\firmware onto the "PlutoSDR" drive and eject it.
FW.dfu_hint: If no DFU device appears: plug in the Pluto while holding the button.
